correctness.rationale: By Raket Theorem 2.1, the exact Gaussian family equals an independent Brownian bridge plus affine endpoints. Conditional strict confinement on arbitrary Gaussian endpoints is the killed/free Brownian heat-kernel ratio. The Dirichlet sine series has first eigenvalue pi squared/(8 tolerance squared), and |sin(n theta)|<=n sin(theta) provides an endpoint-uniform RELATIVE remainder R(tolerance) including near absorbing endpoints. The inverse free heat kernel contributes a multiplier in [1, exp(2 tolerance squared)], establishing the all-matrix sandwich. Rank-0/1/2 Gaussian change-of-variable integrals give the exact constants and establish positivity. Conditioning shifts the moving endpoint Gaussian density by a bounded relative cosine factor, giving O(tolerance squared) total-variation approximation; the rank-changing limit is only weak. The embedded Python standard-library verifier independently checked 2381 assertions; the proof, not finite testing, covers the full quantified claim.

originality.rationale: The motivating pre-anchor Raket bestiary (first public 2026-10-24) catalogues Brownian, anti-periodic, Slepian and other boundary-process examples but does not state the continuous sup-norm small-ball expansion, uniform relative estimate, rank-dependent constants, or cosine-tilted conditional endpoint crossover. The subsequent 2026-10-27 paper gives the independent Gaussian endpoint decomposition and covariance rank strata but not any of those new confinement assertions. Classical killed heat-kernel spectral survival (a proof ingredient), the pinned-bridge and Brownian-motion special cases, Li 1999 logarithmic Markov small-deviation theorem, and Petrova 2019 L2 perturbation work do not individually assert the uniform all-rank crossover statement. Targeted scientific literature and published mathematical-result searches did not identify a directly covering all-covariance theorem. A 2003 survey and classical Slepian/Shepp papers are explicitly recognized as residual priority risks; searches do not prove novelty.

value.rationale: For an existing complete two-parameter endpoint covariance family, controlling a whole continuous-path narrow-tube event is intrinsic and more stringent than finite-dimensional Gaussian likelihood. The exact sharp polynomial small-ball prefactor changes discontinuously in power across all three natural endpoint covariance ranks and cannot be extrapolated at eigenvalue scales comparable to tolerance squared. A single uniform function H supplies a phase crossover for arbitrary moving/singular covariances and a meaningful conditional endpoint shape. It is a natural complete rank classification and rare-event asymptotic, not a numerical slice or textbook individual Brownian special case; no broader theorem-sized consequence is required. Future uses include supremum threshold calibration and endpoint-conditioned rare-trajectory inference.
